trust_decision.summary: Whether a Mollie payment's status is written onto a Sylius order is decided in PaymentWebhookController::__invoke from two independent, unauthenticated request parameters - the Mollie payment id (`id`) and the Sylius order id (`orderId`) - with no check that the Mollie payment belongs to that order, so the status of any payment reachable with the shop's API key can drive the chosen order's last payment state.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the payment webhook; this is the only handler of the /update-payment route, and line 46 is where the order that will be acted on is chosen from the request's `orderId`, while the status comes from a completely unrelated `id` fetch at line 43.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is the post-payment redirect that finishes checkout and hands the browser a Payum token, not the webhook; the report is about payment status and about Mollie's server-side callback, so a solver can call this navigation helper a neighbouring feature - and the same argument covers the QR-code endpoint.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A failed payment is replaced by a new Payment whose details are empty (CaptureAction.php:86,172-186) while the order keeps the earlier Mollie id in its own `molliePaymentId` field (QrCodeAction.php:68 via MolliePaymentIdOrderTrait.php:25-33), so the webhook deliberately updates `$order->getLastPayment()`; a fix that requires the notified Mollie id to equal the last payment's `details['payment_mollie_id']` rejects legitimate notifications for retried and QR-code orders whose link lives on the order or on an older payment.

O6_input_shapes: `id` as a single Mollie payment id read by Request::get, so it may arrive in the query string or the POST form body (src/Controller/Shop/PaymentWebhookController.php:43)
`orderId` as an array (`orderId[]=`) since the parameter bag returns an array for findOneBy(['id' => ...]) (src/Controller/Shop/PaymentWebhookController.php:46)
missing or unknown `orderId` (early HTTP 200 at lines 47-49) and missing `id` (uncaught ApiException at line 43)
a notified Mollie payment that belongs to a different order than `orderId`, and one that belongs to the same order (the case the guard must distinguish)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET|POST /get-code?orderId=<n> returns the saved QR code (and id) of any order, resolved from the client-supplied orderId with no token or session check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a QR-code display helper for the QR payment method that returns only an image URL and changes no payment or order state, so it looks outside the report's payment-status property.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same namespace (Sylius\MolliePlugin\Controller\Shop) as the landing point, one controller file away

O8b_injection_room.sibling: remove-code accepts an arbitrary `orderToken`, resolves the order by token value and mutates it (clears the QR code and optionally the Mollie payment id).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same controller already resolves orders from a client identifier here and from the cart context two methods earlier, so a maintainer copying the orderToken lookup would not notice the missing ownership check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second HTTP status-sync endpoint that resolves a Sylius payment from a client-supplied Mollie payment id and sets its state, mirroring the existing Payum StatusAction.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the plugin already implements status synchronisation over `payment_mollie_id` in src/Payum/Action/StatusAction.php:97-99, so exposing the same logic behind a shop route is a natural-looking duplication.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a webhook/redirect URL builder that appends a signed order token next to (or instead of) the plain order id.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this provider and QrCodeAction.php:150-155 are the only two places that build the `?orderId=` URLs, and a maintainer fixing the IDOR would plausibly add a token parameter to one and forget the other.

O9_family: authorization bypass / insecure direct object reference (CWE-639) - payment-status forgery through an unauthenticated webhook

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare the notified Mollie id with `$order->getLastPayment()->getDetails()['payment_mollie_id']` and return 200 on mismatch: it still reads the same two parameters from the POST body as well as the query string, and it rejects legitimate notifications for retried or QR-code payments whose Mollie id lives on the order (Order::getMolliePaymentId()) or on an older payment.
